To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actin-based transport adapts polarity domain size to local cellular curvature.
the size of cortical Cdc42-Gtp polarity domains in fission yeasts is adapted to local cell curvature, and that this adaptation requires the actin cytoskeleton.

(i) Cdc42-GFP oscillating polarity domains scale with local cell curvature, independently of cell volume, (ii) this scaling depends on the fusion of actin-transported vesicles with the cell membrane, and (iii) actin networks may serve as curvature-sensors to adapt domain size to local cell geometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cell polarity, a fundamental feature of cell biology that is essential for many biological processes.
how cells sense and adapt their shape.
understanding how the size and shape of cells are determined.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size of the Cdc42p domain is set by the balance between the rate of Cdc42-GDP to Cdc42-Gtp conversion by the GEFs and the rate of Cde42-GTP diffusion.
the width of Cdc42p-GTP domains is determined by the local cell-surface radius of curvature.
the width of Cdc42-GFP domains scales with local cell surface curvature, and that this local scaling requires formins and vesicle transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the width of Cdc42-GDP domains in fission-yeast spores is proportional to local cell curvature, and that this scaling is mediated by the fusion of secreted vesicles with the cell cortex.
the width of polarity domains is determined by the geometry of the cell, in particular, by the curvature of its cell surface.
the width of Cdc42-Gtp domains in fission yeasts scales with the radius of curvature of the local cell membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the width of cortical polarity domains can adapt to the local cell-surface geometry.
cell shape may be a determinant of cell polarity and, in turn, cell polarity may be a determinant for cell shape.
actin-based transport can adapt domain size to local cellular curvature.
